title: Sterile neutrinos and the reactor antineutrino anomaly
bottleneck: Reactor experiments measured about 6 percent fewer antineutrinos than flux calculations predicted, hinting at oscillation into a sterile fourth neutrino, but refined flux models and new short-baseline measurements have weakened the case without fully explaining the deficit. The anomaly sits in limbo between new physics and nuclear-physics systematics.
why_it_blocks: A confirmed sterile neutrino would be the first new fundamental fermion in decades and would reshape neutrino cosmology; leaving the anomaly unresolved contaminates precision oscillation measurements that assume only three flavors.
current_state: STEREO, PROSPECT, and DANSS find no oscillation signal, favoring revised flux predictions, but the original deficit and the gallium anomaly keep a weakened sterile hypothesis alive. The gallium anomaly from radioactive-source calibrations keeps a separate sterile hint alive even as the reactor evidence fades.
